monsieur.etymology: F., fr. mon my + Sieur, abbrev. of seigneur lord. See Monseigneur.

monsoon.etymology: Malay musim, fr. Ar. mausim a time, season: cf. F. monson, mousson, Sr. monzon, Pg. monç\'eeo, It. monsone.

monster.etymology: OE. monstre, F. monstre, fr. L. monstrum, orig., a divine omen, indicating misfortune; akin of monstrare to show, point out, indicate, and monere to warn. See Monition, and cf. Demonstrate, Muster.

monstrance.etymology: LL. monstrantia, fr. L. monstrare to show: cf. OF. monstrance. See Monster.

monstrous.etymology: OE. monstruous, F. monstrueux, fr. L. monstruosus, fr. monstrum. See Monster.

monte.etymology: Sp., lit., mountain, hence, the stock of cards remaining after laying out a certain number, fr. L. mons, montis, mountain.

month.etymology: OE. month, moneth, AS. mon, mona; akin to mona moon, and to D. maand month, G. monat, OHG. manod, Icel. manu, mana, Goth. meno. *272. See Moon.

monument.etymology: F., fr. L. monumentum, fr. monere to remind, admonish. See Monition, and cf. Moniment.

mood.etymology: The same word as mode, perh. influenced by mood temper. See Mode.

moon.etymology: OE. mone, AS. mona; akin to D. maan, OS. & OHG. mano, G. mond, Icel. mani, Dan. maane, Sw. måne, Goth. mena, Lith. men, L. mensis month, Gr. mas moon, month; prob. from a root meaning to measure (cf. Skr. ma to measure), from its serving to measure the time. *271. Cf. Mete to measure, Menses, Monday, Month.

moor.etymology: F. More, Maure, L. Maurus a Moor, a Mauritanian, an inhabitant of Mauritania, Gr. Morris a dance, Morocco.

moose.etymology: A native name; Knisteneaux mouswah; Algonquin monse. Mackenzie.

moot.etymology: OE. moten, motien, AS. motan to meet or assemble for conversation, to discuss, dispute, fr. mot, gemot, a meeting, an assembly; akin to Icel. mot, MHG. muoz. Cf. Meet to come together.

mope.etymology: Cf. D. moppen to pout, Prov. G. muffen to sulk.

moraine.etymology: F. Cf. Prov. G. mur stones broken off, It. mora a heap of stones, hillock, G. mürbe soft, broken up, OHG. muruwi, AS. mearu tender, Gr. mla to relax.

moral.etymology: F., fr. It. moralis, fr. mos, moris, manner, custom, habit, way of life, conduct.

morass.etymology: OE. marras, mareis (perh. through D. moeras), fr. F. marais, prob. from L. mare sea, in LL., any body of water; but perh. influenced by some German word. See Mere a lake, and cf. Marsh.

morbid.etymology: L. morbidus, fr. morbus disease; prob. akin to mori to die: cf. F. morbide, It. morbido. See Mortal.

morbific.etymology: L. morbus disease + -ficare (in comp.) to make: cf. F. morbifique. See -fy.

mordacious.etymology: L. mordax, -acis, fr. mordere, morsum, to bite. See Morsel.

mordacity.etymology: L. mordacitas: cf. F. mordacité. See Mordacious.

mordant.etymology: F., p.pr. of mordere to bite; L. mordere. See Morsel.

more.etymology: AS. mor. See Moor a waste.

morello.etymology: Cf. It. morello blackish, OF. morel. Cf. Morelle.

moresque.etymology: F., fr. It. moresco, or Sp. morisco. See Morris.

morganatic.etymology: LL. matrimonium ad morganaticam, fr. morganatica a morning gift, a kind of dowry paid on the morning before or after the marriage, fr. OHG. morgan morning, in morgangeba morning gift, G. morgengabe. See Morn.

moribund.etymology: L. moribundus, from moriri to die. See Mortal.

morion.etymology: F. morion, Sp. morrion; cf. Sp. morra the upper part of the head, morro anything that is round.

morn.etymology: OE. morwen, morgen, AS. morgen; akin to D. morgen, OS. morgan, G. morgen, Icel. morginn, morgunn, Sw. morgon, Dan. morgen, Goth. maúrgins. Cf. Morrow, Morning.

moro.etymology: Cf. It. mora mulberry, L. morum.

morocco.etymology: Named from Morocco, the country. Cf. Morris the dance.

morose.etymology: L. morosus, prop., excessively addicted to any particular way or habit, fr. mos, moris, manner, habit, way of life: cf. F. morose.

roots.meaning: A combining form denoting a discourse, treatise, doctrine, theory, science; as, theology, geology, biology, mineralogy.

morris.etymology: Sp. morisco Moorish, fr. Moro a Moor: cf. F. moresque, It. moresca.

morrow.etymology: OE. morwe, morwen, AS. morgen. See Morn.

morse.etymology: F. morse, Russ. morj'; perh. akin to E. mere lake; cf. Russ. more sea.

morsel.etymology: OF. morsel, F. morceau, LL. morsellus, a dim. fr. L. morsus a biting, bite, fr. mordere to bite; prob. akin to E. smart. See Smart, and cf. Morceau, Mordant, Muse, v., Muzzle, n.

mortal.etymology: F. mortel, L. mortalis, from mors, mortis, death, fr. moriri 8die; akin to E. murder. See Murder, and cf. Filemot, Mere a lake, Mortgage.

mortar.etymology: OE. morter, AS. mortere, L. mortarium: cf. F. mortier mortar. Cf. sense 2 (below), also 2d Mortar, Martel, Morter.

mortgage.etymology: F. mort-gage; mort dead (L. mortuus) + gage pledge. See Mortal, and Gage.

mortification.etymology: F., fr. L. mortificatio a killing. See Mortify.

mortify.etymology: OE. mortifien, F. mortifier, fr. L. mortificare; L. mors, mortis, death + -ficare (in comp.) to make. See Mortal, and -fy.

roots.meaning: A suffix signifying to make, to form into, etc.; as, acetify, amplify, dandify, Frenchify, etc.

mortise.etymology: F. mortaise; cf. Sp. mortaja, Ar. murtazz fixed, or W. mortais, Ir. mortis, moirtis, Gael. moirteis.

mortmain.etymology: F. mort, morte, dead + main hand; F. main- morte. See Mortal, and Manual.

morula.etymology: NL., dim. of L. morum a mulberry.

mosaic.etymology: F. mosaïque; cf. Pr. mozaic, musec, Sp. & Pg. mosaico, It. mosaico, musaico, LGr. musivum; all fr. Gr. Muse the goddess.

moslem.etymology: Ar. muslim a true believer in the Mohammedan faith, fr. salama to submit to God, to resign one's self to the divine will. Cf. Islam, Mussulman.

mosque.etymology: F. mosquée, Sp. mezquita, Ar. masjid, from sajada to bend, adore.

mosquito.etymology: Sp. mosquito, fr. moscafly, L. musca. Cf. Musket.

moss.etymology: OE. mos; akin to AS. meós, D. mos, G. moos, OHG. mos, mios, Icel. mosi, Dan. mos, Sw. mossa, Russ. mokh', L. muscus. Cf. Muscoid.

most.etymology: OE. most, mast, mest, AS. m; akin to D. meest, OS. mest, G. meist, Icel. mestr, Goth. maists; a superl. corresponding to E. more. *103. See More, a.

motet.etymology: F., a dim. of mot word; cf. It. mottetto, dim. of motto word, device. See Mot, Motto.

moth.etymology: OE. mothe, AS. moedhedhe; akin to D. mot, G. motte, Icel. motti, and prob. to E. mad an earthworm. Cf. Mad, n., Mawk.

mother.etymology: OE. moder, AS. modor; akin to D. moeder, OS. modar, G. mutter, OHG. muotar, Icel. moedhir, Dan. & Sw. moder, OSlav. mati, Russ. mate, Ir. & Gael. mathair, L. mater, Gr. mh`thr, Skr. matrs; cf. Skr. ma to measure. *268. Cf. Material, Matrix, Metropolis, Father.

motion.etymology: F., fr. L. motio, fr. movere, motum, to move. See Move.

motive.etymology: F. motif, LL. motivum, from motivus moving, fr. L. movere, motum, to move. See Move.

motley.etymology: OE. mottelee, motle; cf. OF. mattelé clotted, curdled, OF, ciel mattonné a mottled sky, mate, maton, curdled milk, Prov. G. matte curd. Cf. Mottle.

motor.etymology: L., fr. movere, motum, to move.

motorial.etymology: L. motorius that has motion. See Motor, n.

motto.etymology: It. motto a word, a saying, L. muttum a mutter, a grunt, cf. muttire, mutire, to mutter, mumble; prob. of imitative origin. Cf. Mot a word.

mould.etymology: OE. molde, AS. molde; akin to D. mul, G. mull, mulm, OHG. molt, molta, Icel. mold, Dan. muld, Sw. mull, Goth. mulda, and E. meal flour. See Meal, and cf. Mole an animal, Mull, v.

moulder.etymology: From Mold fine soft earth: cf. Prov. G. multern.

mouldy.etymology: From Mold the growth of fungi.

moult.etymology: OE. mouten, L. mutare. See Mew to molt, and cf. Mute, v. t.

mound.etymology: F. monde the world, L. mundus. See Mundane.

mount.etymology: OE. munt, mont, mount, AS. munt, fr. L. mons, montis; cf. L. minae protections, E. eminent, menace: cf. F. mont. Cf. Mount, v., Mountain, Mont, Monte, Montem.

mountain.etymology: OE. mountaine, montaine, F. montagne, LL. montanea, montania, fr. L. mons, montis, a mountain; cf. montanus belonging to a mountain. See 1st Mount.

mountaineer.etymology: OF. montanier, LL. montanarius. See Mountain.

mountebank.etymology: It. montimbanco, montambanco; montare to mount + in in, upon + banco bench. See Mount, and 4th Bank.

mourn.etymology: AS. murnan; akin to OS. mornian, OHG. mornen, Goth. maúrnan.

mouse.etymology: OE. mous, mus, AS. mus, pl. mys; akin to D. muis, G. maus, OHG. & Icel. mus, Dan. muus, Sw. mus, Russ. muishe, L. mus, Gr. my^s, Skr. mush mouse, mush to steal. *277. Cf. Muscle, Musk.

mouth.etymology: OE. mouth, mu, AS. m; akin to D. mond, OS. m, G. mund, Icel. mu, munnr, Sw. mun, Dan. mund, Goth. mun, and possibly L. mentum chin; or cf. D. muil mouth, muzzle, G. maul, OHG. m, Icel. m, and Skr. mukha mouth.

move.etymology: OE. moven, OF. moveir, F. mouvoir, L. movere; cf. Gr. miv, p.p. muta, to move, push. Cf. Emotion, Mew to molt, Mob, Mutable, Mutiny.

movement.etymology: F. mouvement. See Move, and cf. Moment.

mow.etymology: F. moue pouting, a wry face; cf. OD. mouwe the protruded lip.

moxie.etymology: fr. Moxie, a trade name for a beverage.

much.etymology: OE. moche, muche, miche, prob. the same as mochel, muchel, michel, mikel, fr. AS. micel, mycel; cf. Gr. mjök, adv., much. *103. See Mickle.

mucilage.etymology: F., from L. mucilago a musty juice, fr. mucus mucus, slime. See Mucus.

muck.etymology: Icel. myki; akin to D. mög. Cf. Midden.

roots.meaning: A suffix or combining form meaning like, resembling, in the form of; as in anthropoid, asteroid, spheroid.

mucor.etymology: L., fr. mucere to be moldy or musty.

mucus.etymology: L. mucus, muccus; cf. mucere 8be moldy or musty, Gr. muc to release. Cf. Match for striking fire, Moist, Mucilage.

mud.etymology: Akin to LG. mudde, D. modder, G. moder mold, OSw. modd mud, Sw. modder mother, Dan. mudder mud. Cf. Mother a scum on liquors.

muff.etymology: Cf. LG. muff, D. mof, G., Dan., & Sw. muff, F. moufle mitten, LL. muffula, MHG. mouwe sleeve, D. mouw, and E. muffle, v.

muffle.etymology: Cf. F. moufle a mitten, LL. muffula, OD. moffel a muff. See Muff.

mug.etymology: Cf. Ir. mugam a mug, mucog a cup.

muggy.etymology: Cf. Icel. mugga mist, mugginess. Cf. 4th Mold.

muharram.etymology: Ar. muharram, prop., sacred, forbidden, n., the first month of the Mohammedan lunar year.

mulatto.etymology: Sp. & Pg. mulato, masc., mulata, fem., of a mixed breed, fr. mulo mule, L. mulus. See Mule.

mulberry.etymology: OE. moolbery, murberie, AS. murberie, where the first part is fr. L. morum mulberry; cf. Gr. Murrey, Sycamore.

mulch.etymology: Cf. mull dirt, also Prov. G. mulsch, molsch, rotten, soft, mellow, as fruit.

mule.etymology: F., a she-mule, L. mula, fem. of mulus; cf. Gr. m, fr. L. mulus. Cf. Mulatto.

muleteer.etymology: F. muletier, fr. mulet a mule, dim. fr. L. mulus.

muliebrity.etymology: L. muliebritas, fr. muliebris belonging to a woman, fr. mulier a woman.

mull.etymology: Perh. contr. fr. mossul. See Muslin.

muller.etymology: OE. mullen to pulverize, bruise; cf. Icel. mylja; prob. akin to E. mold soil. See Mold soil, and cf. Mull dirt.

mullet.etymology: OE. molet, mulet, F. mulet, fr. L. mullus.

mullion.etymology: A corruption of munnion, F. moignon stump of an amputated limb, stump, OF. moing mutilated; cf. Armor. moñ, mouñ, mank, monk, and also L. mancus maimed.

roots.meaning: A prefix signifying much or many; several; more than one; as, multiaxial, multocular.

multifarious.etymology: L. multifarius; multus much, many. Cf. Bifarious.

multiform.etymology: L. multiformis; multus much, many + forma shape: cf. F. multiforme.

roots.meaning: A prefix signifying much or many; several; more than one; as, multiaxial, multocular.

multinomial.etymology: Multi- + -nomial, as in binomial. See Binomial.

roots.meaning: A prefix signifying much or many; several; more than one; as, multiaxial, multocular.

multiparous.etymology: Multi- + L. parere to produce: cf. F. multipare.

roots.meaning: A prefix signifying much or many; several; more than one; as, multiaxial, multocular.

multipartite.etymology: L. multipartitus multus much, many partitus divided, p.p.: cf. F. multipartite. See Partite.

multiple.etymology: Cf. F. multiple, and E. quadruple, and multiply.

multiplicand.etymology: L. multiplicandus to be multiplied: cf. F. multiplicande.

multiplication.etymology: L. multiplicatio: cf. F. multiplication. See Multiply.

multiply.etymology: F. multiplier, L. multiplicare, fr. multiplex manifold. See Multitude, Complex.

multipotent.etymology: L. multipotens; multus much + potens powerful. See Potent.

multitude.etymology: F. multitude, L. multitudo, multitudinis, fr. multus much, many; of unknown origin.

multivalent.etymology: Multi- + L. valens, p. pr. See Valence.

roots.meaning: A prefix signifying much or many; several; more than one; as, multiaxial, multocular.

mumble.etymology: OE. momelen; cf. D. mompelen, mommelen, G. mummelen, Sw. mumla, Dan. mumle. Cf. Mum, a., Mumm, Mump, v.

mummer.etymology: Cf. OF. mommeur. See Mumm, and cf. Momier.

mummery.etymology: F. momerie, of Dutch or German origin. See Mumm.

roots.meaning: A suffix signifying to make, to form into, etc.; as, acetify, amplify, dandify, Frenchify, etc.

mummy.etymology: F. momie; cf. Sp. & Pg. momia, It. mummia; all fr. Per. m, fr. m wax.

mumps.etymology: Prov. E. mump to be sulky. Cf. Mump, Mumble, and Mum.

munch.etymology: Prob. akin to mumble: cf. also F. manger to eat (cf. Mange), and mâcher to cher (cf. Masticate). See Mumble.

mundane.etymology: L. mundanus, fr. mundus the world, an implement, toilet adornments, or dress; cf. mundus, a., clean, neat, Skr. mansds to adorn, dress, mansdsa adornment. Cf. Monde, Mound in heraldry.

municipal.etymology: L. municipalis, fr. municipium a town, particularly in Italy, which possessed the right of Roman citizenship, but was governed by its own laws, a free town, fr. municeps an inhabitant of a free town, a free citizen; munia official duties, functions + capere to take: cf. F. municipal. Cf. Immunity, and Capacoius.

munificent.etymology: L. munificus; munus service, gift + -ficare (in comp.) to make. Cf. Immunity, -fy.

roots.meaning: A suffix signifying to make, to form into, etc.; as, acetify, amplify, dandify, Frenchify, etc.

munition.etymology: F., munition of war, L. munitio a fortifying, fortification, fr. munire to fortify, defend with a wall; cf. moenia walls, murus (for moirus) a wall, and Skr. mi to fix, make firm. Cf. Ammunition.

munjeet.etymology: Hind. majitsh a drug used for dyeing red.

mural.etymology: F., fr. L. muralis, fr. murus wall. See Mure a wall.

murder.etymology: OE. morder, morther, AS. moredhor, fr. moredh murder; akin to D. moord, OS. moredh, G., Dan., & Sw. mord, Icel. moredh, Goth. maúrþr, OSlav. mreti to die, Lith. mirti, W. marw dead, L. mors, mortis, death, mori, moriri, to die, Gr. broto`s (for mroto`s) mortal, 'a`mbrotos immortal, Skr. mrs to die, mrsta death. *105. Cf. Amaranth, Ambrosia, Mortal.

murine.etymology: L. murinus, from mus, muris, mouse: cf. F. murin.

murky.etymology: OE. mirke, merke, AS. myrce, mirce; akin to Icel. myrkr, Dan. & Sw. mörk.

murmur.etymology: F. murmure: cf. L. murmur. CF. Murmur, v. i.

murrain.etymology: OE. moreine, OF. morine, fr. OF. morir, murir, 8die, L. mori, moriri.

musa.etymology: NL., fr. Ar. mauz, mauza, banana.

muscadel.etymology: It. moscadello, moscatello, LL. muscatellum or muscadellum (sc. vinum), fr. muscatellus nutmeglike, dim. of muscatus smelling like musk, muscatum and muscata (sc. nux) nutmeg: cf. F. muscadelle, fr. Italian. See Musk and cf. Moschatel, Muscardin, Muscat, Nutmeg.

muscle.etymology: F., fr. L. musculus a muscle, a little mouse, dim. of mus a mouse. See Mouse, and cf. sense 3 (below).

mush.etymology: Cf. Gael. mus, muss, pap, porridge, any thick preparation of fruit, OHG. muos; akin to AS. & OS. mos food, and prob, to E. meat. See Meat.

mushroom.etymology: OE. muscheron, OF. mouscheron, F. mousseron; perhaps fr. mousse moss, of German origin. See Moss.

musk.etymology: F. musc, L. muscus, Per. musk, fr. Skr. mushka testicle, orig., a little mouse. See Mouse, and cd. Abelmosk, Muscadel, Muscovy duck, Nutmeg.

musket.etymology: F. mousquet, It. moschetto, formerly, a kind of hawk; cf. OF. mousket, moschet, a kind of hawk falcon, F. mouchet, prop., a little fly (the hawk prob. being named from its size), fr. L. musca a fly. Cf. Mosquito.

muslin.etymology: F. mousseline; cf. It. mussolino, mussolo, Sp. muselina; all from Mussoul a city of Mesopotamia, Ar. Mausil, Syr. Mauzol, Muzol, Mosul, where it was first manufactured. Cf. Mull a kind of cloth.

muss.etymology: Cf. OF. mousche a fly, also, the play called muss, fr. L. musca a fly.

mussitation.etymology: L. mussitatio suppression of the voice, fr. mussitare to be silent, to murmur.

must.etymology: OE. moste, a pret. generally meaning, could, was free to, pres. mot, moot, AS. moste, pret. mot, pres.; akin to D. moetan to be obliged, OS. motan to be free, to be obliged, OHG. muozan, G. müssen to be obliged, Sw. måste must, Goth. gamotan to have place, have room, to able; of unknown origin.

mustache.etymology: F. moustache, It. mostaccio visage, mostacchio mustache, fr. Gr. mostacho.

mustang.etymology: Sp. musteño belonging to the graziers, strayed, wild.

mustard.etymology: OF. moustarde, F. moutarde, fr. L. mustum must, - - mustard was prepared for use by being mixed with must. See Must, n.

muster.etymology: OE. moustre, OF. mostre, moustre, F. montre, LL. monstra. See Muster, v. t.

musty.etymology: From L. mustum must; or perh. fr. E. moist. Cf. Must, n., Moist.

mutable.etymology: L. mutabilis, fr. mutare to change. See Move.

mutation.etymology: L. mutatio, fr. mutare to change: cf. F. mutation. See Mutable.

mute.etymology: L. mutare to change. See Molt.

mutilate.etymology: L. mutilatus, p.p. of mutilare to mutilate, fr. mutilus maimed; cf. Gr. Mutton.

mutiny.etymology: From mutine to mutiny, fr. F. se mutiner, fr. F. mutin stubborn, mutinous, fr. OF. meute riot, LL. movita, fr. movitus, for L. motus, p.p. of movere to move. See Move.

mutter.etymology: Prob. of imitative origin; cf. L. muttire, mutire.

mutton.etymology: OE. motoun, OF. moton, molton, a sheep, wether, F. mouton, LL. multo, by transposition of l fr. L. mutilus mutilated. See Mutilate.

mutual.etymology: F. mutuel, L. mutuus, orig., exchanged, borrowed, lent; akin to mutare to change. See Mutable.

muzzle.etymology: OE. mosel, OF. musel, F. museau muzzle or snout, LL. musellus, fr. musus, morsus. See Muse, v. i., and cf. Morsel.

mya.etymology: L. mya a kind of mussel.

mycelium.etymology: NL., fr. Gr. my`khs a mushroom.

myrobalan.etymology: L. myrobalanum the fruit of a palm tree from which a balsam was made, Gr. myrobolan.

myrrh.etymology: OE. mirre, OF. mirre, F. myrrhe, L. myrrha, murra, Gr. murr bitter, also myrrh, Heb. mar bitter.

myrtle.etymology: F. myrtil bilberry, prop., a little myrtle, from myrte myrtle, L. myrtus, murtus, Gr. m.

mystic.etymology: L. mysticus, Gr. mystique. See 1st Mystery, Misty.

mystical.etymology: L. mysticus, Gr. mystique. See 1st Mystery, Misty.

mystify.etymology: F. mystifier, fr. Gr. -ficare (in comp.) to make. See 1st Mystery, and -fy.
